title: SiDA: Sparsity-Inspired Data-Aware Serving for Efficient and Scalable Large Mixture-of-Experts Models
problem: Serving large Mixture-of-Experts models at scale requires efficient routing and scheduling to handle high throughput while respecting latency constraints. Current systems do not adequately exploit the natural sparsity in MoE models where each token activates only a subset of experts.
motivation: Mixture-of-Experts models enable larger model capacity with conditional computation, but efficient inference serving remains challenging without intelligent exploitation of sparsity patterns.
method: SiDA uses data-aware analysis of input characteristics to inform sparsity-inspired serving decisions. The system employs adaptive routing and batching strategies that exploit expert activation sparsity patterns, combining intelligent token-to-expert routing with memory-efficient scheduling to reduce end-to-end inference latency.
key_novelty: Integrating data-aware serving with sparsity-inspired routing to dynamically adapt MoE inference strategies based on input data characteristics and activation patterns.
contributions: Data-aware serving framework that adapts routing based on input characteristics
Sparsity-optimized scheduling exploiting conditional expert activation
System design achieving improved throughput and latency for large MoE inference
Demonstration of efficient scaling for large-scale mixture-of-experts models
limitations: Not discussed in title; analysis limited to title-only characterization.
primary_theme: efficient MoE inference via sparsity-aware data-driven serving
